name: Nadab
overview: Nadab was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Shammai according to 1 Chronicles 2:28. There are no additional notes or distinctive attributes recorded about him beyond his lineage. His presence in Scripture is primarily genealogical, situating him within the broader family lines of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Nadab means "volunteer" or "free will offering," reflecting a Hebrew proper name not given by God but carrying a meaningful connotation. This meaning may imply a character associated with willing service or dedication, though the biblical text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Nadab as the son of Shammai (1 Chronicles 2:28). It is also inferred from genealogical records that Seled and Appaim were his ancestors, possibly his father or forefathers, as indicated in 1 Chronicles 2:30. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Nadab's significance lies chiefly in his genealogical role within the tribe of Judah, contributing to the lineage that is foundational to Israel's history. His mention in 1 Chronicles situates him within the covenant community and reflects God's providential preservation of His people through family lines. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the importance of faithful lineage in God's redemptive plan.
